pr_body:
When path mapping is enabled, different `Spawn`s in the same build can have identical `RemoteAction.ActionKey`s and can thus provide remote cache hits for each other. However, cache hits are only possible after the first local execution has concluded and uploaded its result to the cache. 

To avoid unnecessary duplication of local work, the first `Spawn` for each `RemoteAction.ActionKey` is tracked until its results have been uploaded and all other concurrently scheduled `Spawn`s wait for it and then copy over its local outputs. 

Fixes #21043
pr_title: Deduplicate locally executed path mapped spawns

review_comment: I think it's worth adding a comment here explaining why this only applies to local executions - for remote executions, we rely on the remote service to deduplicate for us.
Add a comment explaining what motivates this.

The `FileOutErr` is action-scoped, not spawn-scoped (see https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/exec/AbstractSpawnStrategy.java;l=363;drc=d32202b20f82c17f75ee204d505b08f2160640f5), so I think this might incorrectly replay output unrelated to this spawn? Should we first introduce a separate Spawn-scoped `OutErr`?
This is correct, but I think that the distinction ends up not mattering for the path mapping use case. I added a comment explaining this, please let me know what you think.
I think this is good enough for now, thanks.

FYI - I suspect that this has a chance of failing if we ever apply path mapping to test actions with multiple test attempts (which move spawn outputs to a different location after spawn execution). This is already a problem for async uploading, so whatever we end up doing to fix it should also apply here. No need to do anything about it for now.

That's a good catch. At least in its current form, path mapping for test actions wouldn't be very useful as top-level targets that differ in configuration typically do so intentionally, with at least some part of their transitive closure being different (as in, different file content). In this case, path mapping wouldn't help.
Add a `@return` clause to the javadoc, documenting in particular the meaning of `null`.
